title_en: Xu Yongbei v. Jiangsu Provincial Daily Chemical Research Institute — dispute over bonuses and incentive fees
keywords_en: civil; reward fee dispute; bonus distribution dispute; second instance; intermediate people's court; Jiangsu Province; natural person; legal person; Regulations on Awards for Scientific and Technological Progress; Interim Provisions of the State Council on Technology Transfer; General Principles of Civil Law; bonus distribution proportion; extraction of technology transfer reward fees; determination of contribution size; partial support; research and development of scientific projects; transfer of technological achievements; bonus distribution dispute; reasonable distribution based on contribution size
full_text_en:
Xu Yongbei v. Jiangsu Daily Chemical Research Institute

— dispute over bonus and reward fees

Plaintiff: Xu Yongbei, male, 51 years old, senior engineer at Jiangsu Nanjing Daily Chemical Research Institute.

Defendant: Jiangsu Daily Chemical Research Institute.

Legal Representative: Lu Rugang, Director.

Third Party: Zheng Wenshen, male, 47 years old, engineer at Jiangsu Daily Chemical Research Institute.

Third Party: Gong Huifen, female, 49 years old, engineer at Jiangsu Daily Chemical Research Institute.

The plaintiff, Xu Yongbei, filed a lawsuit with the Nanjing Xuanwu District People's Court of Jiangsu Province against the defendant, Jiangsu Daily Chemical Research Institute, concerning a dispute over bonuses and reward fees. After reviewing the complaint, the court, in accordance with Article 48, paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (for Trial Implementation), added Zheng Wenshen and Gong Huifen, who jointly developed the "New Process and New Equipment for Continuous Emulsification of Cosmetics" with the plaintiff, as third parties to participate in the proceedings.

The plaintiff alleged: During his work at the defendant's unit, he participated in the research and development of the "New Process and New Equipment for Continuous Emulsification of Cosmetics" and served as the team leader, playing a major role in the development process. The state-issued bonus for this scientific research achievement still had RMB 4,000 that the defendant refused to distribute. After the defendant transferred this technology and received a technology transfer fee of RMB 300,000, it has failed to provide the plaintiff with reward fees in accordance with regulations. The plaintiff requested that the defendant distribute bonuses and reward fees to him in accordance with laws and policies.

The defendant argued: The defendant repeatedly notified the plaintiff to negotiate the distribution of the bonus, but the plaintiff failed to appear as scheduled, resulting in the RMB 4,000 bonus remaining undistributed. The technology transfer fee received by the defendant was not as high as the plaintiff claimed, and the plaintiff did not participate in the technology transfer work and therefore had no right to demand reward fees.

The third parties, Zheng Wenshen and Gong Huifen, stated: Although the plaintiff served as the team leader, he did not fulfill his duties to the fullest extent. The distribution of bonuses should follow customary practice, with the unit retaining 30% and the remainder distributed equally. The plaintiff did not participate in the technology transfer work and had no right to demand reward fees.

After a public hearing, the Xuanwu District People's Court found the following facts:

The plaintiff, Xu Yongbei, was originally a researcher at the Jiangsu Daily Chemical Research Institute. In October 1981, the defendant decided to establish a research group consisting of the plaintiff and the third parties to develop the "New Process and New Equipment for Continuous Emulsification of Cosmetics" (hereinafter referred to as the "New Emulsification Equipment"), with the plaintiff serving as the team leader. In June 1982, the Jiangsu Provincial Department of Light Industry, the Science and Technology Commission, and the Department of Finance formally assigned this research project. The "New Emulsification Equipment" was successfully developed in March 1983 and passed the technical appraisal of the Jiangsu Provincial Department of Light Industry. When reporting this technological achievement to the higher authorities, the defendant truthfully evaluated the work of the plaintiff and the third parties, affirming the plaintiff's contributions as the team leader. In September 1983, the "New Emulsification Equipment" research project was awarded a second-class scientific research prize by the Ministry of Light Industry of the State, receiving a bonus of RMB 1,000. This bonus was distributed under the plaintiff's leadership, with the defendant retaining 24% as expenses for rewarding other personnel, the plaintiff receiving 18%, third parties Zheng Wenshen and Gong Huifen each receiving 13%, four support staff receiving 12%, and a collaborating unit receiving 20%. In October 1985, the "New Emulsification Equipment" research project was also awarded a third-class National Science and Technology Progress Prize, receiving a bonus of RMB 5,000. After deducting the RMB 1,000 bonus received in 1983 as required, the actual bonus was RMB 4,000. The plaintiff and the defendant negotiated the distribution of this bonus multiple times but failed to reach an agreement due to differing opinions.

In November 1985, the defendant entered into a technology transfer contract for the "New Emulsification Equipment" with Wuxi County Tractor Parts Factory of Jiangsu Province. The Wuxi County Tractor Parts Factory paid the defendant a technology transfer fee of RMB 200,000 and a supervision fee of RMB 14,400. The plaintiff transferred out of the defendant's unit in March 1986 and did not participate in the technology transfer or supervision work. The defendant did not withdraw reward fees in accordance with state regulations and, during the trial, failed to provide evidence of the costs of the technology transfer as required by the court.

The Xuanwu District People's Court held: The "New Emulsification Equipment" was successfully developed by the plaintiff and the third parties upon the defendant's decision. According to Article 1 of the Regulations on Science and Technology Progress Awards of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the "Regulations"), which stipulates "awards to collectives and individuals who have made important contributions in promoting scientific and technological progress," the plaintiff, the defendant, and the third parties all have the right to claim the state-issued bonus. Article 12, paragraph 2 of the Regulations provides: "The bonuses for science and technology progress awards shall be distributed reasonably according to the size of contributions. Those who have made significant contributions shall be heavily rewarded, and egalitarianism shall not be practiced." When reporting the "New Emulsification Equipment" technological achievement to the higher authorities, the defendant affirmed the plaintiff's contributions as the team leader. The plaintiff's request to distribute the bonus according to the size of contributions is lawful and should be supported. The defendant's denial of the plaintiff's contributions during the litigation, along with the third parties' proposal for equal distribution of the bonus, lacks legal basis and is not supported.

After the defendant transferred the "New Emulsification Equipment" technology, it should have, in accordance with Article 7, paragraph 2 of the Interim Provisions of the State Council on Technology Transfer (hereinafter referred to as the "Provisions"), which states: "The unit transferring the technology shall withdraw 5-10% from the retained net income from technology transfer as reward fees, to be distributed under the direction of the research group leader, without interference from the unit itself or other relevant departments," withdrawn a proportional amount of reward fees to reward the personnel directly involved in the research and development of the technology. However, the defendant failed to fulfill its legal obligation, and its conduct violated Article 106, paragraph 1 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China. Article 97, paragraph 2 of the General Principles of the Civil Law provides: "Citizens have the right to apply for and obtain certificates of honor, bonuses, or other rewards for their inventions or other scientific and technological achievements." The plaintiff's claim for receiving bonuses and reward fees in accordance with the law should be supported. The third parties did not specify specific amounts for the bonuses and reward fees they should receive, indicating a willingness to negotiate with the defendant on their own, which should be permitted. Accordingly, on June 22, 1989, the Xuanwu District People's Court ruled:

1. For the Science and Technology Progress Award of RMB 4,000 for the "New Emulsification Equipment" research project, plaintiff Xu Yongbei shall receive RMB 1,400, and the remainder shall be distributed among the defendant and the third parties on their own.

2. From the net income of the technology transfer fee, 10% shall be withdrawn as reward fees, totaling RMB 21,440, of which plaintiff Xu Yongbei shall receive RMB 8,576, and the remainder shall be distributed among the defendant and the third parties on their own.

After the first-instance judgment was pronounced, the defendant and the third parties, Zheng Wenshen and Gong Huifen, all appealed to the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province. The defendant's grounds for appeal were: (1) The RMB 4,000 bonus should be distributed in the same proportion as the original RMB 1,000 bonus, and the amounts for Zheng Wenshen and Gong Huifen should be specified; (2) The supervision fee of RMB 14,400 should not be included in the technology transfer fee, and the reward fees should only be withdrawn at 5% from the net income after deducting technology transfer costs; (3) Xu Yongbei did not participate in the technology transfer work and has no right to share in the technology transfer reward fees; such reward fees should only be obtained by the defendant and the third parties. Zheng Wenshen and Gong Huifen's grounds for appeal were: (1) Xu Yongbei exaggerated his role in the development; they requested an increase in the bonus distribution ratio and a clear determination of the bonus amounts; (2) Xu Yongbei did not participate in the technology transfer work and has no right to share in the technology transfer reward fees; they requested a clear determination of the reward fee amounts the third parties should receive.

During the second instance, the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court, based on evidence provided by the appellant, Jiangsu Daily Chemical Research Institute, found that the technology transfer costs amounted to RMB 24,243.85.

The Nanjing Intermediate People's Court held: The "New Emulsification Equipment" was a job-related technological achievement jointly developed by the appellee, Xu Yongbei, and the appellants, Zheng Wenshen and Gong Huifen. During the development, Xu Yongbei served as the team leader and played a major role, which was affirmed in the appellants' report on the technological achievement to the higher authorities. The first-instance court's ruling that Xu Yongbei should receive RMB 1,400, in accordance with the Regulations' provision that bonuses for scientific and technological achievements should be distributed according to the size of contributions without practicing egalitarianism, was not improper. The appellants' denial of Xu Yongbei's major role is unfounded. The distribution plan for the RMB 1,000 bonus, which was formulated by Xu Yongbei and to which no party objected at the time, only reflects the parties' free disposition of their civil rights regarding that specific matter and cannot serve as the basis for distributing the RMB 4,000 bonus in dispute. The appellants' current request to clarify the specific bonus amounts each should receive is an exercise of their civil rights in accordance with the law and should be supported.

Although the appellee, Xu Yongbei, did not directly participate in the technology transfer work, according to Article 4 of the Provisions, as a "personnel directly involved in the research and development of the technology," he has the right to apply for and receive reward fees. Furthermore, according to the same provision, Zheng Wenshen and Gong Huifen are both "personnel directly involved in the research and development of the technology" and "meritorious personnel who assisted the transferee in effectively mastering the transferred technology during the technology transfer," and thus they may appropriately receive a higher amount of reward fees. The appellants Zheng Wenshen and Gong Huifen's request to clarify the specific reward fee amounts they should receive should also be permitted. Article 4 of the Provisions also states: "For technologies researched and developed in implementation of national or superior plans, unless otherwise provided for in the plans for promotion and application, the completing unit may also transfer them in accordance with these Provisions, and the transfer income shall belong to the unit." The appellant Jiangsu Daily Chemical Research Institute, as the unit transferring the technology, has already received the technology transfer fee and should not share in the technology transfer reward fees. The first-instance judgment's ruling that, after deducting the amount received by Xu Yongbei from the technology transfer reward fees, the defendant should also receive a portion of the reward fees was clearly inappropriate. The appellant Jiangsu Daily Chemical Research Institute's request to clarify the specific reward fee amount it should receive lacks legal basis and is not supported.

As for the appellant Jiangsu Daily Chemical Research Institute's ground for appeal that the supervision fee of RMB 14,400 should not be included in the technology transfer fee, with reference to the State Science and Technology Commission's "Explanation on Certain Specific Policies of the Technology Market," supervision may be considered as technical services provided by the transferor to the transferee, and its income may be included in the net income from technology transfer. During the first instance, because Jiangsu Daily Chemical Research Institute refused to provide evidence of the technology transfer costs, the first-instance court was unable to calculate the net income from technology transfer. After deducting the now-established technology transfer costs of RMB 24,243.85 from the total technology transfer fee and supervision fee of RMB 214,400, the net income should be RMB 190,156.15. The first-instance court's determination to withdraw 10% as technology transfer reward fees complies with the State Council's regulations.

Accordingly, on June 15, 1990, the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court, in accordance with Article 151, paragraph 1, item 2 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (for Trial Implementation), ruled as follows:

1. Amend paragraph 1 of the first-instance judgment to read: "For the Science and Technology Progress Award bonus of RMB 4,000 for the 'New Emulsification Equipment' research project, appellee Xu Yongbei shall receive RMB 1,400, appellant Jiangsu Daily Chemical Research Institute shall receive RMB 1,200, Zheng Wenshen shall receive RMB 750, and Gong Huifen shall receive RMB 650."

2. Amend paragraph 2 of the first-instance judgment to read: "From the net income of the technology transfer fee, reward fees totaling RMB 19,015.61 shall be withdrawn, of which Xu Yongbei and Zheng Wenshen shall each receive RMB 6,655.82, and Gong Huifen shall receive RMB 5,703.97."
